narrative.title: The Hardware Token Allocator
narrative.scenario: A compute cluster hands out GPU tokens to queued jobs: each job states the minimum token strength it will accept, and each token has a fixed strength. A job accepts at most one token, and a token serves at most one job. The scheduler wants to satisfy as many jobs as possible, matching the weakest acceptable token to each waiting job.
narrative.inputFormat: Two integer arrays: g (each job's minimum acceptable strength) and s (each token's strength).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the maximum number of jobs that can be satisfied.

testCases.explanation: Both tokens are strength 1, so only the greediest-of-three's weakest demand can be met.
Tokens 1 and 2 cover both jobs; the spare token sits unused.

hintLevels: Level 1: Waste the smallest acceptable resource on the easiest demand — never over-spend a big token early.
Level 2: Sort both arrays; walk tokens left to right, advancing the job pointer on each match.
Level 3: The job pointer only moves forward on success, so tokens too weak for the current job are useless for it and everyone after.
